source_text:
De trinitate
̓Επιφανίου Κύπρου ἐκ τοῦ περὶ τριάδος λόγου.
Μία δοξολογία πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος καὶ μία προσκύνησις·
ὅτε γὰρ δοξολογοῦσι τὰ σεραφὶμ τὸν θεὸν "ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος", πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν καὶ
πνεῦμα ἅγιον δοξολογοῦσι.
pass_a_gloss: Lemmatic heading naming Epiphanius of Cyprus and his treatise about the triad. Then a single ascription of splendor to all three — Father together with Son together with Holy Ghost — plus one single act of adoration. The supporting reason: whenever the burning ones sing splendor to the Almighty using the threefold shout of holiness, those identical three persons receive that song.
pass_b_english: Of Epiphanius of Cyprus, from the discourse On the Trinity.
One glorification of Father and Son and Holy Spirit, and one worship; for when the seraphim glorify God with "Holy, holy, holy" (Isaiah 6:3), they glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

choices.choice: Inline parenthetical beside the triple Holy; Revelation 4:8 echoes the same chant.
Both rendered definite; the articles vary but the referent is the same three persons.

notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify
